newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB seen relaxed despite dip in mark/Swiss.
newsitem.headline: SNB seen relaxed despite dip in mark/Swiss.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) may attach less importance than it has in past to keeping the Swiss franc in check versus the mark, given the franc's sharp drop against the dollar, analysts said.
Although the mark on Wednesday dropped to 81.05 centimes, its lowest level since late August 1996, the dollar on Thursday rose to 3-1/2 year highs of around 1.50 francs.
In the past 12 months the mark traded as low as 80.47 centimes on August 27, rising from there to 87.77 on February 20, 1997. Since then it has generally declined.

Much of the mark's earlier gains were attributed to efforts by the SNB to keep its policy generous, in order to weaken the franc. The mark's latest weakness is seen partly tied to uncertainties about the start of the single European currency.

The SNB, as expected, left its discount rate at 1.00 percent at Thursday's weekly board meeting. The rate has been kept at the current level since September 26, 1996, when it was cut from 1.50 percent.
CSFB analyst Michael Bernegger said given the SNB's current inaction, it was possible the mark could dip to 80.00 centimes.
The mark's lowest level in the past five years was 79.75 set on September 21, 1995.
"Overall, mark/Swiss should resume its sharp downtrend amid overall mark weakness, and apparent SNB passivity quite soon," said currency analysts at CSFB in a daily market comment.
Bernegger said that the chances were greater that the SNB's next move would be a tightening rather than an easing, even though he saw no urgency for any such action now.
Some economists believe the SNB will keep rates on hold at least until late this year.

Germany is Switzerland's main trading partner, accounting for 23 percent of Swiss exports in the first half of 1997. This makes the mark a currency of major importance in Switzerland's efforts to pull out of a protracted economic slump.

But currency analysts said even though the mark has taken a pounding lately, allowing the Swiss franc to rise to its highest levels in roughly 11 months, the SNB may be reassured somewhat by the Swiss currency's weakness versus the dollar.
"The pressure on the SNB is somewhat less than was the case a year ago," said one Swiss economist at a major bank.
He and other economists also say that the SNB may be watching the "trade-weighted" Swiss franc rather than mark/Swiss per se.
The nominal trade-weighted level on Thursday at 154.13 (1977 = 100). On a monthly basis the lowest level for the index in 1997 so far was in February at 149.2.

In 1996 the highest level was 164.3 set last August, when the SNB embarked on an aggressive campaign to lower money market rates in order to counter the Swiss franc's rise. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
